title: ADJUDICATE (human): move bd store off flat-file RMW (per-worker stores + merger, or dolt/sqlite backend)
description: Structural follow-up from biod: the shared BEADS_DIR store is a git working tree written by 7 worker processes + sync loop + janitor, with checkpoint commits and rewinding normalizations guarding it. The layered mitigation (pre-commit hook blocking worker-side store staging + per-branch checkpoints, a158b0ffd7) makes loss practically unreachable, but file-copy granularity remains the disease (worker-4's words). Human decision: (a) keep current architecture and accept the residual, (b) per-worker bd stores with a merger pass in the sync loop, or (c) move bd to its dolt/sqlite backend (check bd's storage options and migration cost first; AGENTS.md forbids bd dolt push — local-only dolt is unaffected). Evidence thread: project-LICHEN-worker6-biod, worker-4's measured incidents.
close_reason: Decision: keep the flatfile architecture with the shipped mitigations (a158b0ffd7: pre-commit hook blocking worker-side store staging + per-branch checkpoints in sync/janitor). Rationale: all 3 measured incidents were the git-rewind mechanism, which the mitigations close; bd flatfile (v1.1.0-flatfile.2, brew) has internal file locking for process-level RMW; option (b) per-worker stores breaks global claim semantics (bd ready/claim need the shared pool); option (c) dolt backend is a non-standard build for this fleet and dolt already proved unstable here (Attic panic in dolt-server.log). Investigated the 'dolt keeps restarting' suspicion: NOBODY restarts it — the running dolt sql-server (PID 1048711, 27 days old, port 36815, zero clients) belongs to another heft user (langwei), and our .beads/dolt-server.pid/port files are stale debris git-synced from the macOS Attic store (claims dead pid 42946/port 53901; bd flatfile provably never touches them). Revisit (c) only if a NEW loss incident appears post-hook that is not the rewind mechanism — recheck after a week of fleet runtime.
